title: 2026 NFL Fantasy Waiver Wire Week 3: Jonah Coleman & Bryce Young Top Targets on NFL.com
body:
The fantasy‑football landscape is already shifting as Week 3 looms, and savvy managers are eyeing the waiver wire for hidden gems that could turn a middling roster into a playoff contender. Among the most talked‑about names are Denver’s breakout running back Jonah Coleman and Carolina’s rookie quarterback Bryce Young, both of whom have shown flashes of elite production and are now available to teams willing to act quickly. As injuries mount and early‑season expectations settle, the waiver market is becoming a critical battleground for owners looking to solidify depth at running back, quarterback and other key positions.

Coleman’s ascent has been nothing short of meteoric. After a modest start to his rookie campaign, the 22‑year‑old burst onto the scene with a 115‑yard, two‑touchdown performance against the New York Giants, followed by a 102‑yard effort in a narrow loss to the Buffalo Bills. Those back‑to‑back 100‑yard games have lifted his usage rate to roughly 34 % of Denver’s snaps, a figure that now rivals veteran back Javonte Williams. More importantly, Coleman’s explosive play‑making ability—evidenced by a 4.8 yards‑per‑carry average and a 0.48 touchdown per attempt ratio—makes him a prime candidate for fantasy owners seeking a high‑upside RB2 or even a flex option. With the Broncos’ offensive line showing signs of cohesion and the team leaning heavily on the ground game to complement Russell Wilson’s passing attack, Coleman’s workload is expected to remain robust, especially as Denver navigates a schedule that includes several run‑heavy opponents in the coming weeks.

Across the league, rookie quarterback Bryce Young is generating a different kind of buzz. The former Alabama Heisman finalist entered the NFL with lofty expectations, and while his early outings have been a mixed bag, the Panthers’ 20‑year‑old has already posted a 113.3 passer rating and an 8.9 yards‑per‑attempt average—statistics that outpace many veteran starters in comparable situations. Young’s most recent start against the Atlanta Falcons highlighted his poise under pressure; he completed 21 of 30 passes for 276 yards, two touchdowns, and no interceptions, while also contributing a 12‑yard rush. Though his completion percentage sits at a modest 70 % against expectations, the underlying metrics suggest a quarterback who can elevate his play when the offensive line gives him time. With Carolina’s receiving corps still coalescing around veteran WRs and emerging talents, Young’s ability to stretch the field could provide fantasy managers with a low‑risk, high‑reward waiver acquisition, especially in leagues that reward passing yards and touchdown passes heavily.

Running backs remain the most volatile position on fantasy rosters, and the waiver wire is littered with players who could become weekly starters due to injuries or strategic shifts. Beyond Coleman, names such as Jacksonville’s James Cook and Seattle’s Kenneth Walker III have surfaced as viable RB2 options, each offering a blend of receiving upside and goal‑line work. However, Coleman’s recent performance curve and the Broncos’ commitment to a run‑first philosophy give him a distinct edge. For owners with limited bench spots, scooping up Coleman now could also serve as a hedge against potential injuries to Williams or the team’s primary backfield options later in the season.

Quarterback depth is equally precarious, particularly in leagues that start two QBs or reward multi‑position flexibility. While established starters like Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen dominate the top tiers, the waiver market provides an avenue to secure a backup with upside. Bryce Young’s early numbers, coupled with Carolina’s willingness to let him gain experience, make him a compelling addition for owners needing a fill‑in during bye weeks or a spark for a struggling starter. Moreover, Young’s dual‑threat capability—averaging over 4.5 yards per rush—adds a layer of fantasy value that pure pocket passers often lack.

Looking ahead, the waiver wire will likely continue to churn as Week 4 approaches, with teams like the Buffalo Bills and the Los Angeles Rams expected to release depth pieces after evaluating their early‑season rosters. Fantasy managers who stay attuned to injury reports, snap counts and coaching adjustments will be best positioned to capitalize on these opportunities. Whether it’s locking down Jonah Coleman as a reliable RB2 or grabbing Bryce Young as a low‑cost quarterback with upside, the key will be decisive action before competing owners snap up the talent. As the NFL season gains momentum, the waiver wire may prove to be the decisive factor separating championship contenders from the rest of the pack.
